items.title: v1.0.1
items.summary: ## What's changed? PyRIT `v1.0.1` is a patch release with a single targeted bug fix. It contains no new features and no intentional breaking changes; upgrading from `v1.0.0` should be a drop-in replacement for nearly all users. **Reason for the patch:** OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions can return *structured refusals* — a valid model response that carries a refusal explanation instead of ordinary text content. PyRIT treated these as parser/runtime failures. In practice that meant a refusal from the target could leave attack objectives incomplete and surface a misleading scenario-level `ValueError`, rather than being recorded and scored as the refusal it actually was. ### You should upgrade if you - Use `OpenAIResponseTarget` or `OpenAIChatTarget` against models that emit structured refusals (this is common with recent OpenAI and Azure OpenAI models). - Run scenarios that can legitimately be refused by the target — refusals no longer abort the atomic attack, and genuine partial execution now raises the dedicated `ScenarioPartialFailureException` with structured counts, the incomplete objectives, and the original cause. - Rely on true/false scorers — a syntactically valid but ou

items.summary: ## What's Changed ### New features * Feature: technique and intent annotation and initial IntentProbe iteration by `garak-maintainers` in https://github.com/NVIDIA/garak/pull/1984 "Power is in tearing attacks to pieces and putting them together again in shapes of your own choosing." This initial feature represents the first step in enabling users to provided their own context and requirements for target expectations and enable identification of attack vectors that show the edges of the underlying systems safeguards and runtime posture from new perspectives. This feature includes the initial groundwork for bringing user context into account during evaluation of a target. In its first iteration, it provides a new facet of information while keeping the existing probes primarily unchanged. The _trait_ and _intent_ concepts are explored, with _policy_ introduced only as a reference definition. Further iteration and community feedback will guide how these new concepts are consumed, and influence how the broader Context Aware Scanning feature evolves. * arch: support & data for trait/intent, and for policy datatype by @leondz in https://github.com/NVIDIA/garak/pull/1421 * cas feature: int

items.title: Add CITATION.cff and the 2026 Zenodo DOI (#124)
items.summary: Add CITATION.cff and the 2026 Zenodo DOI (#124) * Add CITATION.cff and automated Zenodo deposit for the 2026 edition Papers already cite the Top 10 (NVIDIA's garak paper cites the first version), but with no DOI there is no identifier for Crossref, OpenAIRE or Google Scholar to resolve against, so finding that use means manual searching. This adds citation metadata and a workflow that deposits each edition to Zenodo, which mints the DOI. CITATION.cff carries the authors of the 2026 entries. GitHub renders it as "Cite this repository", and the release workflow builds the Zenodo record from it, so the author list is maintained in one place rather than two. .github/zenodo.config.json holds the file list for each deposit. `{edition}` comes from the release tag, so the 2027 edition needs no config change. Each key under `deposits` is a separate Zenodo record, so any future publication from this repo can take its own concept DOI instead of becoming a version of the Top 10. .github/scripts/zenodo_release.py builds the bundle and deposits it through the Zenodo REST API, with `--check` to validate the config and CITATION.cff, `--dry-run` to print the file list, and `--sandbox` to target san

items.title: v1.1.0
items.summary: ## What's changed? PyRIT `v1.1.0` improves scoring, expands scanner capabilities, and adds major CoPyRIT features. Python support remains `>=3.10, <3.15`. ### ⚠️ Breaking changes - Scores can now be undetermined. Check `score.is_undetermined` before reading `score_value` or calling `get_value()` ([#2491](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/pull/2491)). - Partial blocked responses are now scored by default. Set `should_score_blocked_content=False` to retain the previous behavior. - Authenticated CoPyRIT deployments now use Microsoft Graph and require an allowed group configuration ([#2281](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/pull/2281)). - The new fixed-egress CoPyRIT deployment requires a parallel Azure Container Apps environment. items.title: vLLM : DoS via unvalidated mm_processor_kwargs in multimodal image processors (Isaac, InternVL, H2OVL, etc.)
items.summary: ## Summary API clients can supply arbitrary `mm_processor_kwargs` per request. vLLM forwards these values through the multimodal rendering and processing pipeline to Hugging Face and custom image/video processor constructors and calls. Resource-sensitive values such as image size, patch size, patch count, crop count, or frame count can therefore be controlled by a remote client. items.title: vLLM: Forged multimodal UUID + P0/P1 processor-cache eviction drift: unauthenticated remote crash of the whole vLLM engine
items.summary: ## Summary Multimodal content parts (`image_url`, `video_url`, `input_audio`, ...) accept a user-supplied `uuid` field that vLLM uses **verbatim as the item's cache identity** (`mm_hash`). The two frontend/engine processor caches (P0 "sender" cache in the API process, P1 "receiver" cache in the EngineCore process) are independent LRU caches whose evictions are **not synchronized**, and the P1 hit path performs **zero consistency validation** — it silently substitutes the cached item's tensor data for whatever the current request actually contains. A single unauthenticated client can exploit this to kill the entire engine, deterministically, with default server flags: 1. **Seed**: send a small image with `uuid="U"`. Both caches now map `U` to an item with **N_A** visual tokens (e.g. 4). 2. **Drift**: send ~70 requests, each carrying a *unique* uuid, a max-size image, and an over-long text prompt. Each request is rejected with 400 — but **after** its image has been inserted into the P0 cache (insertion happens during chat rendering, before prompt-length validation), so these requests fill P0 **without ever reaching the engine/P1**. `U` is evicted from P0 only. 3. **Kill**: send a *la

items.title: virtualenv: Bash activator leaves the --prompt value unescaped in PS1 when promptvars is off, so prompt expansion later executes it (regression in 21.14.9)
items.summary: ## Summary The bash activator puts the caller-supplied prompt value into `PS1` unescaped whenever `promptvars` is off at activation time, and assumes prompt expansion can never run afterwards. `promptvars` and posix mode are runtime shell state, not a property of the activation moment: re-enabling prompt expansion in the same shell (`shopt -s promptvars`, `set -o posix`) or starting an interactive child bash that inherits the exported `PS1` makes bash expand the stored value and run the command substitution in it. An attacker who controls the prompt value gets command execution as the user who sources `bin/activate`. This is a regression. 21.14.8 escaped `$` and the backtick unconditionally and stays inert under the same sequence. The 21.14.9 fix for GHSA-6w3r-xr62-4xcp (#3418) rewrote that block and left bash with a path that stores the raw value whenever `promptvars` is off. ## Affected area Activation scripts (activate, activate.bat, activate.csh, activate.fish, activate.nu, Activate.ps1, activate.xsh) — specifically the bash `bin/activate`. ## Attacker-controlled input The `--prompt` value, which the security policy already lists as a value that may come from project metadata t

items.title: FastMCP MCP client wrappers construct M2M OAuth providers without issuer binding — client secret redirectable to attacker-advertised authorization server
items.summary: ## Maintainer assessment and remediation This report is accepted as a FastMCP credential-binding vulnerability. Affected versions of the OAuth client credentials providers do not expose the authorization-server issuer that owns pre-registered credentials. An untrusted or compromised MCP server can therefore advertise a different authorization server and receive the client secret or a signed assertion. Signing keys themselves remain local; assertion replayability depends on the assertion source and audience policy. Affected stable versions are 4.0.0–4.1.1 of `fastmcp` and `fastmcp-slim`. The wrappers were introduced in 4.0.0a1; 3.x does not include them. The 4.1.2 fix adds `issuer` to `ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider` and `PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider` and requires MCP SDK 2.2.0. It also discards refresh credentials from reloaded tokens: without persisted authorization-server metadata, inherited refresh could otherwise transmit credentials before issuer discovery, including when a cached token was valid at startup and expired later. Cached tokens are isolated by configured issuer, so configuring or changing the issuer acquires a new token. Valid cached access tokens for the same issuer

items.title: FastMCP: Post-transform component authorization is skipped on direct calls
items.summary: ## Maintainer assessment and remediation This report is accepted as a FastMCP authorization vulnerability. In supported configurations, a server transform can change the metadata used by a component's authorization policy. Direct lookups previously checked the original component but returned the transformed component without rechecking its policy. A client that knows the component identifier can invoke a tool or retrieve a resource or prompt that the configured policy denies. The fixes authorize the final transformed tools, resources, templates, and prompts. A denied concrete resource also shadows a matching resource template at its URI, preventing proxy templates from retrieving the same protected resource upstream. Authorized callers, authorized component versions, and templates for genuinely absent concrete resources remain supported. Affected stable release lines: FastMCP 3.0.0–3.4.9 and 4.0.0–4.1.1. The missing final authorization check is present in v3.0.0 history and was reproduced on v3.4.9 and v4.1.0.
